units.title: The quadratic fiber score has exact relative Fisher energy
units.statement: Let ν be the common measure used in the two quadratic normalizers and let μ be any probability law on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. For η≠0 and centers y,y′, the μ-relative Fisher energy of this explicit normalized quadratic log-ratio representative is exactly η⁻²‖y−y′‖². In the source specialization, ν is the common Gibbs base and μ is its left restricted-Gaussian fiber.
assumptions: The common normalization measure ν and the probability integration law μ are separate parameters. In the source, μ is the left tilt of ν.
The integration law μ is a probability measure; this is what turns the integral of a constant into the same constant.
The state space is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and η is nonzero. The paper's fiber variance satisfies η>0.
The argument evaluates the displayed smooth log-ratio representative. It does not differentiate Mathlib's canonical measurable llr representative.

steps.title: Insert the exact score
steps.text: The preceding ASTIS theorem differentiates the displayed quadratic representative genuinely and gives a vector independent of x.

steps.title: Expose the constant integrand
steps.text: Substituting the score in the definition of relative Fisher information leaves a spatially constant squared norm.

steps.title: Use probability mass one
steps.text: Because μ has total mass one, integrating this nonnegative constant does not introduce a mass factor.

steps.title: Pull the scalar out of the norm
steps.text: The norm of a real scalar multiple is its absolute value times the norm. Squaring removes the sign and gives the exact η⁻² coefficient.

units.lean_statement: The function supplied to RelativeFisher.information contains both ν-normalizers explicitly, while the Fisher integral is taken under the separate probability law μ. The normalizers disappear only through the previously proved genuine gradient theorem.
units.lean_proof: The proof unfolds the ASTIS relative-Fisher definitions, rewrites every pointwise gradient with the compiled quadratic-score theorem, and lets Mathlib evaluate the constant integral under the probability instance and normalize the scalar norm square.

sources.label: Smoothed Picard HMC, Lemma 4.17
sources.scope: This exact Fisher value is one analytic input to the cited restricted-Gaussian W₂ contraction route.

boundary: This theorem does not identify the Fisher information of an arbitrary canonical llr representative.
It does not prove a log-Sobolev inequality, Talagrand inequality, Wasserstein contraction, Markov-kernel contraction, or any SPHMC main theorem.

The left law is assumed to be a probability measure and is kept distinct from the common normalization base. Construction and normalization of the actual restricted-Gaussian fiber remain separate adapters.

tests.scope: The paper domain η>0 specializes the reusable η≠0 theorem and the axiom print guards the proof kernel.

review.scope: The repaired two-measure interface, exact coefficient, left probability specialization, explicit-representative boundary and absence of an LSI/T₂/W₂ conclusion were accepted.
